pr_title: Make Difficulty Adjust mod customisation menu open automatically
pr_body:
Closes #7514

Other mods need to overwrite `RequiresConfiguration` property to make customisation menu open automatically on selection.
pr_comments: As mentioned, please add a test to `TestSceneModSettings`

- Add a test mod with the new boolean.
- Select the test mod.
- Ensure the customisation panel opened.
DId I do it right? I was unable to run tests for some reason, so I'll wait until the AppVeyor check finishes.
Do I still need to improve the test?
Would be great, yeah. Looks like that was missed before merge.

issue_context.title: Difficulty adjustment panel should open automatically
issue_context.body:
**Describe the new feature:** 

Difficulty adjustment panel should open automatically when adding a mod that supports adjustments, and "Customize" button should be removed because it is completely redundant.

The fact that a user adds Difficulty Adjust mod already signifies that they wish to drag sliders that adjust the beatmap. It is inconvenient to click a button to reveal what should already be visible.
comments:
> "Customize" button should be removed because it is completely redundant.

Object. This can cause inconvenience on mobile devices if we apply such a change.
I tend to agree with this. Maybe `Mod` can expose a `RequiresConfiguration` bool which can be set in such cases, causes the configuration to be displayed on selection.

> "Customize" button should be removed because it is completely redundant.

Still needs a toggle as the window will block mod buttons on the right.

The thing is, Difficulty Adjust *requires* customisation to make it purposeful. So there's no reason to not have it automatically open on selecting. The user can close it once they are done changing the options.

review_comments: From a code readability prespective, since there is more than one `if` statement here, would be better to add empty line between each line.

This test case needs more work:

* Need to also test that deselecting all mods after selecting with customisation hides the settings
* Running this test twice will cause it to fail the second time since the customisation mod remains selected between test runs

Could you describe what sort of issues you're having with running the tests so we can help resolve them? It's not really a good idea to write tests blindly without being able to run them, kind of defeats the purpose of the entire endeavour.
